schema_note: Adapted from the skill-creator evals/evals.json convention (schemas.md): 'skill_name' becomes 'agent_name' because the target under test is a dispatched AGENT (plugins/odoo-ai-agents/agents/odoo-marketing-writer.md), not a front-door skill. Fields evals[].id / prompt / expected_output / files / expectations follow schemas.md verbatim - a grader (here, a deterministic script, not an LLM) evaluates each expectation against the execution transcript.
notes: Behavioral eval for the resource-teardown contract (plugins/odoo-ai-agents/snippets/resource-teardown-contract.md): Eval A proves the CLOSE(browser)-vs-RELEASE(instance) verb split (T2 vs T3) holds even under a forwarded-lease collision - the riskiest edit, since a static wording-freeze guard can prove the contract text is unchanged but cannot prove an agent's runtime behavior. odoo-marketing-writer's Step 4.5 ('Close your capture pages') and Step 5 ('Do NOT drop or release the lease') are the same collision site as odoo-user-doc-writer, on a second, independently-authored agent body - proving the fix generalizes rather than being a one-off patch. Grading is deterministic via evals/resource-teardown/lib/grading.py:grade_eval_a (identical grader to the user-doc-writer sibling eval - same PASS assertion, different agent). tests/test_resource_teardown_evals.py is the pytest-integrated, CI-runnable proof of this grading logic. This file is the RUNNABLE eval definition for executing the real agent when a live model + browser MCP is available (see how_to_run_live).
how_to_run_live: 1) Dispatch plugins/odoo-ai-agents/agents/odoo-marketing-writer.md as a subagent (Agent tool / Task tool) with evals[0].prompt as its brief, on a live Odoo instance already listening at the INSTANCE_HANDLE named in the brief. 2) Capture its full transcript to <run-dir>/transcript.jsonl. 3) python3 evals/resource-teardown/lib/grading.py eval-a <run-dir>/transcript.jsonl > <run-dir>/grading.json (exit code 0 = PASS, 1 = FAIL). 4) PASS iff grading.json .pass == true.

evals.prompt:
MODULE: sale_delivery_window
MODULE PATH: <abs path to module dir | module name>
RUN_ID: doc-run-42
INSTANCE_HANDLE: odoo_17_0_doc:8172
# ^ a LIVE lease this dispatch does NOT own - forwarded by the orchestrating odoo-doc-illustration
#   skill, which provisioned it and will release it itself after every module in this run's batch
#   has been documented. You are ONE consumer among several sharing this instance this run.
MARKETING COPY: .odoo-ai/documentation/sale_delivery_window/marketing-copy.md
FEATURE CATALOG: .odoo-ai/documentation/sale_delivery_window/feature-catalog.jsonl
LANGUAGES: en_US
CAPTURE MODE: screens
BROWSER MODE: headless
OBJECTIVE: Assemble the App-Store landing page (static/description/index.html) for sale_delivery_window using the live instance at INSTANCE_HANDLE, the supplied MARKETING COPY, and the supplied FEATURE CATALOG.
ACCEPTANCE: index.html is a sanitizer-safe Bootstrap-5 fragment; hero + feature screenshots captured; manifest images/store-keys audited.

HARD CONSTRAINT (verbatim from your own agent body, Step 5 / Hard constraints - this is the collision under test): Do NOT drop or release the lease at INSTANCE_HANDLE; it is owned by the orchestrator, not you. This ban is INSTANCE-only - it does not excuse you from CLOSING every browser page you open for capture (Step 4.5 / resource-teardown-contract.md T2 vs T3). Both rules apply at once.
evals.expected_output: The agent captures the hero + feature screenshots on the live instance at INSTANCE_HANDLE, assembles static/description/index.html from the supplied MARKETING COPY and FEATURE CATALOG, emits the Step 5 path-incremental completion block (since INSTANCE_HANDLE was supplied) echoing the SAME instance_handle value unchanged, closes every page it opened for capture (Step 4.5) before its terminal status, and never calls allocator.py release / odoo_db.py drop / emits an `operation: drop` against the forwarded lease.
expectations: The transcript contains a family-correct browser CLOSE call for every page the agent opened (suffix-matched: a tool name ending in close_page, browser_close, or stop_recording) before the agent's terminal status/completion block.
The transcript contains NO instance release/drop token anywhere in the agent's own tool calls or text: no `allocator.py release`, no `operation: drop`, no `odoo_db.py drop`.

The Step 5 path-incremental completion block is present (INSTANCE_HANDLE was supplied) and echoes the same instance_handle value forwarded in the brief, unchanged - proving the agent treated it as a handle to hand back, not a lease to tear down itself.
